title: Boiled Bean Dumplings
subtitle: filled with black beans and mushrooms, cooked in greens
description: Soft spelt and white bean flour dumplings filled with black beans and portobello mushrooms, simmered in garlicky spinach and chard then finished in the oven.

steps.text: Make the dough: dissolve the yeast in the water in a mixer bowl, add the spelt flour, bean flour, maple syrup, olive oil and salt and knead with the dough hook for about 8 minutes until soft and firm. Add a little more spelt flour if sticky. Cover with a damp towel and prove for 30 to 40 minutes until almost doubled.

Soak the black beans in plenty of water for 12 hours, changing the water halfway, then drain and rinse. Cover with plenty of water and cook for about 50 minutes until very soft and almost falling apart. Drain.

Heat the olive oil in a large pan, fry the chopped onion for 7 to 8 minutes until golden. Add the chopped mushrooms and crushed garlic, then the salt, pepper, maple syrup and chopped parsley, and cook, stirring, for about 8 minutes until the mushrooms brown and release liquid. Add the cooked beans, cook 8 more minutes, then remove from the heat and cool.
Divide the dough into balls slightly smaller than ping-pong balls, flatten each on your palm, put a teaspoon of filling in the middle and close the edges over it. Pinch to seal and roll into a ball.

Heat the olive oil in a wide, low pot and fry the sliced garlic and chopped chilli for about 2 minutes. Add the spinach, chard, salt and pepper and cook for about 6 minutes until the leaves soften. Add the stock (or water), cover and cook for 5 minutes.

Remove the lid, arrange the dumplings in the pot, cover and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes. Preheat the oven to 170°C, then transfer the pot to the oven and bake for 20 more minutes partly covered.
